incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: PROD · proxy_canary_latency (us-east-1) — threshold 1200ms. Rule: synthetic-canary-heartbeat. PD link: https://pagerduty.example/INC12345

sam: acked. I'm the oncall, taking a quick look.

tara: saw a blip on canary graphs about 2m ago, might be the synthetic runner.

ben: incident-bot also shows an auto-resolve window configured — might be noisy. Are we seeing real user impact?

sam: checking service logs and user traffic now. No increase in 5xx. tailing recent proxy logs for spikes.

sam: quick check (local):
```
kubectl -n canary logs deploy/canary-runner --since=10m | grep -i error | tail -n 50
```

leo: I can see the canary runner restarted around 13:01:12, produced a burst of synthetic requests while it warmed up. The requests have tag: x-canary: true.

sam: good catch. Can we confirm the alert rule is not excluding canary-tagged traffic?

ops-bot: PD note: "pagerduty: Incident INC12345 auto-resolved at 1725123568" :information_source:

ben: that matches — PD auto-resolved ~80s after firing. Looks like the system dropped back within the suppression window.

tara: no customer-facing errors reported in Sentry or support queue. I scanned the last 30m — nothing.

sam: conclusion: transient synthetic-canary spike due to test-runner restart. No customer impact. Action items: exclude canary-tagged requests from proxy latency alert, and add runbook step for canary runner restarts.

ben: filing follow-up: REINF-893 (Adjust synthetic-canary alerting & tagging). I'll include the grep snippet and the canary pod restart time. https://jira.example/browse/REINF-893

leo: also recommending a short backoff for the runner on restart to avoid immediate burst. I'll open a PR on the canary repo.

sam: marking as handled. Handoff: normal oncall resumed. No SLA/customer impact; no pager escalation required. Closing thread after follow-up ticket created. :white_check_mark: 

ops-bot: Note added to PD incident INC12345: "Investigated — synthetic canary spike due to runner restart. No customer impact. Follow-up REINF-893."
